name: ramdisk
description: THE CONTROL PANEL RAM DISK IS TAKEN UP AND MOUNTED WRITABLE AT /ram5.  BRAM asks for a 256 KB RAM disk (rdMinRam/rdMaxRam $36/$37 = 8, 32 KB units; run.py rewrites the checksum).  MAME's IIgs has 8 MB, the case where ROM 3 fails to create RAM5 (ProBoot.src's CreateRAM5), so ramdisk.mod has the ROM's MakeDisk make it -- `512 blocks ... (made)' -- replaces the empty Pascal volume the ROM leaves with a ProDOS one, and registers it as /dev/ram0; /etc/rc mounts it with mount_prodos -o write.  The staged rc.local creates /ram5/b1 during the boot, so b1 in the listing is a write through the mount, and df naming /dev/ram0 on /ram5 is the mount itself.  WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: keeping the disk across a soft reboot.  A warm_reset_frame run made the disk again on the second boot and stalled at the system logger, and run.py's own notes say MAME's reset line does not give a working warm reset (apple/fgx#120), so that property is unmeasured here.  Without the BRAM setting the module logs `ramdisk: none' and makes nothing, which every other test's boot shows.
